blocks.intro: Semi-modals — phrases that we use like modals:
items: **Have to** and **need to** change for person and tense like normal verbs and have infinitives.

blocks.text: We form questions with modal verbs like this:

rows.example: Tom **could** read when he was two years old.

blocks.text: We use **be able to** to form other tenses.

blocks.correct: It's useful **to be able to** order things by e-mail. (infinitive)
blocks.incorrect: It's useful **to can** order things by e-mail.

items: Soon, I'll **be able to** speak Italian quite well. (future)
Have you **been able to** speak English for a long time? (present perfect)

rows.example: **Can / Could / May** I use the phone?
You **can / may** send the fax when you like.

blocks.text: **May** is more polite than **could** and **could** is more polite than **can**.
